title: Chris Bloomstran VALUEx BRK 2026
description:
Berkshire Could Fall 99.3% and Still Have Beaten the S&P 
The Semper Augustus founder on Geico's deliberate 80% retreat in premiums starting in 1985, and why Greg Abel's real task is to deploy Berkshire's $270B war chest when the next crisis arrives.

See the full stream of the event here: https://youtube.com/live/V3V7bqLGP9o
summary: The speaker argues that Berkshire Hathaway's long-term success stems from Warren Buffett's ability to pivot at proper moments, such as closing the textile business in 1985 and reducing exposure to overvalued assets like Coca-Cola in 1998. He further contends that recent market interpretations of Berkshire's results as 'awful' are misleading, noting that GEICO's improved underwriting discipline and growth in policy in force were achieved despite a competitive auto insurance environment that will likely result in lower combined ratios in the coming year.
